interest: Shows 1941 debate over freezing Japanese assets to protect American investments in Japan, and Japanese capital in Mexican firms.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.503112, with associated papers under 812.5034 and 894.5034) documents Japanese foreign economic activities and the treatment of international capital between October 1940 and March 1941. It includes a cross-reference sheet indexing a report from Ambassador Josephus Daniels in Mexico regarding Japanese financial interests in four Mexican-registered petroleum, drug, and commercial enterprises. The file also contains an extensive policy memorandum prepared by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs for Assistant Secretary of State Dean Acheson regarding recommendations by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo to freeze Japanese assets and restrict fund transfers from the United States in retaliation for Japanese exchange controls and industrial mobilization measures that froze American corporate balances in Japan.
